name: IntuneManagement - Read-only inventory
purpose: Read Intune configuration profiles, compliance policies, applications and settings catalog policy metadata. Optionally inventory managed devices. Display and export a sanitized report without changing tenant objects.

parameters.name: IncludeDevices
parameters.label: Include managed device inventory
parameters.help: Reads a restricted set of device inventory fields using the shared 365 session. Select Extended read permissions before login for DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All. Device names are included; recovery/bypass codes and user contact details are excluded.

outcomes: Policy and application inventory, collection counts, and optional device records.
Per-collection status so access failures are distinguishable from empty results.
Local Markdown and JSON files with LLM processing instructions.
notes: No policy or tenant setting is changed.
This is a scoped inventory. It does not include assignments, effective policy or every settings catalog value.

The shared Graph SDK session and discovered tenant are reused across reports. Logout / clear session or closing the launcher disconnects its session; independent Microsoft/browser sign-in sessions are separate.
Find reader app is read-only. Register reader app is a separate, explicitly confirmed setup action; administrators review consent and roles separately.
prerequisites: Windows, PowerShell 7, the Microsoft.Graph.Authentication module and access to public Microsoft Graph. Use the separate local dependency installer if the module is missing.
Select Extended read permissions before Login to 365 for Intune collection. Complete the normal Microsoft login window; the launcher discovers your username and tenant before it unlocks reports.
No username, tenant ID, application ID or device code is required in report parameters. The default Microsoft Graph PowerShell client is available without creating a custom app.
The read permissions listed in Technical details, an Intune license, and an account with visibility into the intended scope.
steps: Choose Login to 365 and verify Logged in as and the displayed customer tenant. The verified session is reused across reports.
Optionally select Include managed device inventory.
Choose Run report. Collection uses the existing session; Microsoft may require another normal login if tenant policy or session expiry requires it.
Review Report and Record table, then use Open report folder for the readable and structured output. Inspect incomplete collections before drawing conclusions.
guide.overview: Review Intune configuration profiles, compliance policies, applications and settings catalog policy metadata. Optionally include a limited device inventory.
